profile.summary: LigandMPNN designs amino acid sequences for a protein backbone that is given to it, and unlike earlier methods of its kind it also reads the non-protein atoms around that backbone: small molecules, nucleotides and metals. The input is a PDB file, the output a set of designed sequences with per-sequence confidence figures, and optionally packed side chain conformations so binding interactions can be inspected. The published package also serves ProteinMPNN, SolubleMPNN and two membrane-labelled models from the same code.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract; README.md: first paragraph, Available models

summary_quotes.text: we describe a deep learning-based protein sequence design method called LigandMPNN that explicitly models all non-protein components of biomolecular systems
LigandMPNN generates not only sequences but also sidechain conformations to allow detailed evaluation of binding interactions.
This package provides inference code for [LigandMPNN](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.12.22.573103v1) & [ProteinMPNN](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.add2187) models.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Design is autoregressive over the backbone graph, in the manner of ProteinMPNN, with the ligand atoms added as context. The LigandMPNN checkpoints are built with 32 neighbour edges and 25 context atoms per residue, which is what the names ligandmpnn_v_32_005_25 and the like record. The atom context can be switched off with a flag, which the README offers as a way to see how much the ligand atoms move the amino acid probabilities, and side chain context can be switched on. A separate side chain packing checkpoint produces the side chain conformations.
sections.source_locator: README.md: Available models, examples 21 and 22, Side chain packing model; get_model_params.sh comments

quotes.text: Setting `--ligand_mpnn_use_atom_context 0` will mask all ligand atoms. This can be used to assess how much ligand atoms affect AA probabilities.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four LigandMPNN checkpoints are published, differing in the Gaussian coordinate noise used in training: 0.05, 0.10, 0.20 and 0.30 Angstrom. The same download script also fetches four ProteinMPNN checkpoints, four SolubleMPNN checkpoints, two membrane-labelled models and the side chain packing model, all from files.ipd.uw.edu. A result must name the checkpoint, the model type, the sampling temperature and the seed, since the README is explicit that no seed means a random seed and that running again gives different results. The default model type of run.py is ProteinMPNN, not LigandMPNN.

quotes.text: `--seed` Not selecting a seed will run with a random seed. Running this multiple times will give different results.
`--temperature 0.05` Change sampling temperature (higher temperature gives more sequence diversity).

sections.title: What is reported about it
sections.body: The preprint reports native backbone sequence recovery for residues that touch other molecules: 63.3 per cent against 50.4 per cent for Rosetta and 50.5 per cent for ProteinMPNN near small molecules, 50.5 against 35.2 and 34.0 near nucleotides, and 77.5 against 36.0 and 40.6 near metals. Separately, the HyInv report used LigandMPNN as one of ten published baselines on backbone-only inverse folding panels, where it is the strongest of the ten by average scTM (0.8555), and the smallest gap to HyInv (0.018 on average). These are their authors' figures, not Rewire's.
sections.source_locator: Paper abstract; HyInv report Section 5.2, Table 6 and Table 7

quotes.text: LigandMPNN significantly outperforms Rosetta and ProteinMPNN on native backbone sequence recovery for residues interacting with small molecules (63.3% vs. 50.4% & 50.5%), nucleotides (50.5% vs. 35.2% & 34.0%), and metals (77.5% vs. 36.0% & 40.6%).
LigandMPNN is run on backbone coordinates only.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Inverse folding model: designs sequences for a given backbone, conditioned on the surrounding non-protein atoms, with optional side chain packing.

quotes.text: a deep learning-based protein sequence design method called LigandMPNN that explicitly models all non-protein components of biomolecular systems

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Message-passing network over the backbone graph with autoregressive decoding, as in ProteinMPNN, extended with ligand atom context: 32 neighbour edges and 25 context atoms in the released checkpoints.
facts.source_locator: get_model_params.sh comments; README.md: first paragraph, scoring section

quotes.text: Get probabilities/scores for backbone-sequence pairs using autoregressive probabilities: p(AA_1|backbone), p(AA_2|backbone, AA_1) etc.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A PDB file, parsed with ProDy so residue indices, chain letters and insertion codes are kept. Options can fix residues, choose which to redesign, and bias amino acids by residue index such as A23 or B42D.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Running the code, Main differences compared with ProteinMPNN

quotes.text: Input PDBs are parsed using [Prody](https://pypi.org/project/ProDy/) preserving protein residue indices, chain letters, and insertion codes.

Adding bias, fixing residues, and selecting residues to be redesigned now can be done using residue indices directly, e.g. A23 (means chain A residue with index 23), B42D (chain B, residue 42, insertion code D).

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: FASTA and PDB files of designed sequences, with overall_confidence and ligand_confidence per sequence, and sequence recovery over the redesigned residues. The side chain model writes packed side chains; a scoring mode writes probabilities per position.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Main differences compared with ProteinMPNN; scoring section

quotes.text: Model writes to fasta files: `overall_confidence`, `ligand_confidence` which reflect the average confidence/probability (with T=1.0) over the redesigned residues

facts.value: Not reported. The checkpoint names give the graph size and context size (32 edges, 25 atoms) and the training noise, but no parameter count appears in the files read.

notes: Points for a reviewer. No parameter count, training set or length limit is published in the repository, so those facts are marked unreported or unextracted; the preprint's methods were not read, only the Europe PMC abstract, and the preprint carries no licence in Europe PMC. The weights_url values in the structured rows are the files.ipd.uw.edu URLs that get_model_params.sh fetches, for example https://files.ipd.uw.edu/pub/ligandmpnn/ligandmpnn_v_32_005_25.pt. This record overlaps a ProteinMPNN record: the same package and the same download script serve ProteinMPNN, SolubleMPNN and two membrane-labelled checkpoints, and the HyInv report evaluates ProteinMPNN separately. The HyInv figures are that project's own evaluation, on backbone coordinates only, so they do not test the ligand context that is this model's purpose. Quotes from the HyInv report come from a pdftotext text layer, so line breaks inside them follow the PDF layout.
